bull_bear.body:
- Recognised as a leading manufacturer of centrifugal castings in India, with deep expertise in heat-, wear- and corrosion-resistant alloy solutions and static castings for critical-use environments
- Over five decades of operating legacy (established 1972) and backing of the Neterwala Group, which spans Metallurgy, Software, Speciality Chemicals, Engineering, Geology, Oil & Gas and Environmental solutions
- R&D depth with active technical partnerships with IIT Bombay, IIT Madras, IIT Dharwad and IISc Bengaluru for advanced material characterisation and metallurgical research
- Qualification/approval barrier: actively pursuing product approvals and enlistments from leading global technology licensors, an entry barrier once secured
- High benchmarks on quality and on-time delivery described by management as providing a competitive edge; right-first-time manufacturing culture with operator self-inspection, in-process checks and process audits
- Manufacturing digitalisation and automation - IoT-enabled Spectro analysis, digital quality systems, advanced welding technologies, TPM, and an SQCDPR framework with OEE, MTBF, MTTR, material yield and OTIF KPIs
- Supply-chain resilience built deliberately: three independent LPG supply sources to guarantee zero production downtime, multi-sourcing of critical materials, strategic stockpiling and regional sourcing
- Process innovation lowering cost: optimised manufacturing processes to maximise utilisation of in-house generated materials and existing inventory, significantly reducing material costs while maintaining stringent quality standards
- Very low leverage and strong liquidity described qualitatively by management (Debt Equity 0.03 and Current Ratio 5.60 versus 0.08 and 2.69 in the prior year)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price volatility — Management names volatility in raw material prices as one of the two key risks identified. Uni Abex's alloy castings are nickel- and other-alloy intensive, so input cost swings hit margins directly. Mitigation disclosed: sourcing from multiple suppliers to ensure supply continuity and cost-effective procurement, active monitoring of raw material markets, strategic inventory positions, strategic stockpiling of critical materials and long-term arrangements with major suppliers.
- Foreign exchange exposure on imports and exports — Foreign exchange rate movements may affect the Company's international business, including material imports and goods exports - a structural exposure given the deliberate push into MENA, North America and Asia-Pacific export markets. Mitigation disclosed: hedging measures through contractual arrangements, with forex exposures continuously reviewed.
- Macroeconomic and geopolitical shocks, including the Middle East conflict and tariffs — Management flags that unexpected shifts in the economic environment can impact operations and profitability, that the war in the Middle East threatens to disrupt growth and disinflation, and that material changes such as tariffs, the current war situation and linked commodity processes may put uncertainty in the business environment which may affect the financial position. The exposure is doubled-sided because MENA is both a target growth region and the source of the geopolitical disruption; energy commodity prices are projected to rise 19% in 2026 with oil up 21.4%.
- Tightening environmental regulation and carbon border compliance — Increasing environmental concerns and the tightening of related regulations are placing additional pressure on manufacturers, especially in managing emissions and waste, and compliance with these evolving norms could lead to higher operational costs which may affect overall industry performance. For an exporter this extends to carbon border regimes - the Company reports having achieved CBAM compliance during the year.
- Skilled technical manpower shortage, particularly welders — The Company reports having had to address skilled welder shortages by recruiting from technical institutes and providing 2-3 week structured on-the-job training to build an internal talent pool. With a total permanent workforce of only 103 employees as at 31 March 2026, availability of specialised welding and metallurgical skills is a genuine constraint on scaling output and on executing the planned Bay-3 expansion.
- Energy and critical-input supply disruption — The Company experienced LPG supply disruptions during the year and mitigated them by establishing three independent private supply sources to guarantee zero production downtime. Melting and heat-treatment operations are energy-intensive, so continuity of fuel and power supply is a direct production risk.
- Customer, geographic and end-use concentration with project-order cyclicality — Management explicitly cites diversification across customers, geographies and end-use industries as the means of reducing concentration risk and market cyclicality - an acknowledgement that the exposure exists. Revenue is driven by a relatively small number of large project orders (execution of large orders from NFL, NRL and CPCL named as a driver of the year's performance, against a record order book of approximately Rs.77 crore), and demand is concentrated in petrochemical, fertiliser and refinery reformer applications, making revenue lumpy and tied to those sectors' capex cycles.
- Broad business and economic risks identified by the Board — The Board's risk management policy states the Company, like all business in the country, is exposed to business and economic risks arising out of war, market conditions, vagaries of monsoon, tariffs and commodity risks. The Board has identified risks and steps to mitigate them, with the executive management operating an adequately defined risk-management framework.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Uni Abex specialises in the manufacture of premium alloy steel castings, particularly for decanters and reformer tubes, with a product portfolio spanning radiant tubes, retort tubes, air injection tubes, tube support castings, tube sheets and header assemblies. It supplies high-durability components for demanding applications across industries including fertilisers, refining, direct reduction of iron, hydrogen and ammonia, combining centrifugal casting with static castings for high-performance, critical-use environments. The Company positions itself on a quality-first approach, timely delivery, productivity improvement and industry-approved welding procedures, supported by in-house R&D and academic collaborations.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Reformer / process tubes and assemblies:** Reformer tubes, Reformer catalyst tubes, Radiant tubes, Retort tubes, Air injection tubes, Tube support castings, Tube sheets, Header assemblies
- **Decanter:** Alloy steel castings for decanters
- **Materials / alloys:** R-Alloy (new material commercialised in FY 2025-26 with successful customer deliveries)
- **Segments named by management:** Petro, Decanter, OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer)
business.title: Products & brands

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Shift from component supplier to trusted engineering and materials solutions partner - recommending the right metallurgical solution and collaborating earlier in the customer's engineering cycle to create differentiated value in mission-critical applications
- Growth through applications rather than products: expand the application base of centrifugal castings into niche engineering sectors such as power generation, where material integrity, high-temperature performance and long service life are critical, and grow the separation (decanter centrifuge) business by leveraging metallurgical expertise into adjacent high-value applications
- Selective international expansion - focus on markets where technical capability offers clear differentiation (MENA, North America, Asia-Pacific) via deeper engagement with customers, EPC companies, technology licensors and process designers, rather than pursuing growth for its own sake
- Expand presence on global technology licensors' Approved Vendor Lists as a stated strategic priority, to strengthen credibility and gain access to larger international projects
- Capacity enhancement through the plant expansion (Bay-3) to support increasing demand from global markets and specialised applications
- Continued focus on automation, digital manufacturing and data-driven process control to improve productivity, consistency, quality and responsiveness; developing an end-to-end automated reformer production line and expanding low-cost automation
- Application-led R&D: next-generation alloy development, optimising reformer catalyst tubes for longer service life in fertiliser and refinery use, advanced alloys for ethylene and ammonia cracking, and development of proprietary heat-, wear- and corrosion-resistant alloys
- Digitalisation of the finance function - integrated reporting, enhanced analytics and an ongoing SAP implementation to strengthen controls, reporting accuracy and decision support
- Disciplined capital management: strategic asset monetisation (Thane land), prudent treasury management with proceeds deployed in mutual funds and fixed deposits, and disciplined investment evaluation
- Risk management embedded in financial strategy - active monitoring of raw material markets, strategic inventory positions, forex hedging, long-term supplier arrangements, and diversification across customers, geographies and end-use industries to reduce concentration risk
- People strategy - strengthen employer branding, develop specialised talent, expand campus hiring (METLeap), deepen engagement (METEngage survey), and run the Darwinbox HRMS across payroll, recruitment and performance
- Stated go-forward priorities: deepen customer partnerships, accelerate application-led innovation, strengthen manufacturing excellence and execute with discipline
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Board has approved a capital outlay of Rs.121 crore towards strengthening the Company's production and operational capabilities, described in the Chairman/CFO commentary as planned capital expenditure for FY 2026-27 focused on the Bay-3 expansion. Management frames this as capacity enhancement through plant expansion to support increasing demand from global markets and specialised applications, and points to significant value-creation opportunities from the Bay-3 expansion, automation initiatives, a new manufacturing facility and continued investments in specialised petrochemical and catalyst tube applications. Alongside the physical expansion, the Company is developing an end-to-end automated reformer production line, expanding low-cost automation and strengthening digital manufacturing capabilities to support future capacity expansion, with continued investment in automation, TPM, IoT-enabled Spectro analysis, digital quality systems and advanced welding technologies. A SAP implementation is under way to integrate operational and financial systems. On the operating side FY 2025-26 saw total pouring volume rise 11% to 4,172 MT with the highest melting output achieved in two consecutive months, pull-boring productivity improved from 8 to over 10 tubes per day, and 150 assemblies fabricated with 170 dispatched in March 2026. No commissioning date, completion date or capacity addition figure is disclosed for Bay-3 or for the new manufacturing facility, and R&D capital expenditure for the year is stated as Rs. Nil.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Robust demand from petrochemical and reformer sectors was the stated driver of the year's record sales; Petro and Decanter were the key segments driving sales growth, with the OEM segment also showing respectable order-book growth
- Better product mix and improved selling price realisation, plus improved manufacturing efficiency, were named as the levers behind the improvement in profitability
- Strong execution of large orders from NFL, NRL and CPCL supported the year's performance
- Management sees value-creation opportunities ahead from the Bay-3 expansion, automation initiatives, the new manufacturing facility and continued investment in specialised petrochemical and catalyst tube applications
- Industry expected to benefit from technological advancement - adoption of cutting-edge technology promoting effective and sustainable production, reducing waste and improving production efficiency
- Global high-performance alloy market of USD 10.99 billion in CY 2025-26 projected to reach USD 18.52 billion by CY 2034, driven by additive manufacturing adoption, renewable energy expansion, electronics growth and demand for next-generation aircraft
- Global centrifugal casting market of USD 1.5 billion in CY 2025-26 projected to reach USD 2.2 billion by CY 2033, driven by automotive, aerospace, defence and industrial machinery demand
- Expanding use of high-performance alloys in oil and gas extraction, thermal processing, petroleum and power generation, including manufacturing of industrial gas turbine components, is expected to support industry growth in coming years
- Headwind flagged by management: tightening environmental regulations on emissions and waste could raise operating costs and affect industry performance
- Headwind flagged by management: the war in the Middle East threatens to disrupt growth and disinflation; tariffs, the war situation and linked commodity processes may create business-environment uncertainty affecting the financial position
- Record order book of approximately Rs.77 crore, described by management as providing strong visibility for future growth
- Secured the largest-ever project order from the fertilizer sector (largest-ever order from NFL)
- Won a major order for a petrochemical refinery in the MENA region; secured the highest-value customer order from the Middle East
- First-ever export order from the refinery segment
- First-time catalyst tube orders from both India and the MENA region
- Orders received from a major petroleum company and a leading DRI producer in the MENA region
- Expanded the customer base in the separation industry through new decanter centrifuge accounts
- Commercialised Thermalloy 64 MR reformer tubes through an order from a leading fertilizer company in India, and commercialised the new R-Alloy material with successful customer deliveries
- The Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) segment witnessed respectable growth in the order book

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Uni Abex Alloy Products Limited, established in 1972 and part of the family-owned Neterwala Group, is recognised as a leading manufacturer of centrifugal castings in India, supplying high-durability heat-, wear- and corrosion-resistant alloy components for critical industrial applications.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Uni Abex specialises in the manufacture of premium alloy steel castings, particularly for decanters and reformer tubes, with a product portfolio spanning radiant tubes, retort tubes, air injection tubes, tube support castings, tube sheets and header assemblies. It supplies high-durability components for demanding applications across industries including fertilisers, refining, direct reduction of iron, hydrogen and ammonia, combining centrifugal casting with static castings for high-performance, critical-use environments. The Company positions itself on a quality-first approach, timely delivery, productivity improvement and industry-approved welding procedures, supported by in-house R&D and academic collaborations.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Reformer / process tubes and assemblies:** Reformer tubes, Reformer catalyst tubes, Radiant tubes, Retort tubes, Air injection tubes, Tube support castings, Tube sheets, Header assemblies
- **Decanter:** Alloy steel castings for decanters
- **Materials / alloys:** R-Alloy (new material commercialised in FY 2025-26 with successful customer deliveries)
- **Segments named by management:** Petro, Decanter, OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Fertilisers (largest-ever order from the fertiliser segment secured in FY 2025-26; NFL named as customer)
- Refining / petroleum (first export order from the refinery segment)

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Robust demand from petrochemical and reformer sectors was the stated driver of the year's record sales; Petro and Decanter were the key segments driving sales growth, with the OEM segment also showing respectable order-book growth
- Better product mix and improved selling price realisation, plus improved manufacturing efficiency, were named as the levers behind the improvement in profitability
- Strong execution of large orders from NFL, NRL and CPCL supported the year's performance
- Management sees value-creation opportunities ahead from the Bay-3 expansion, automation initiatives, the new manufacturing facility and continued investment in specialised petrochemical and catalyst tube applications
- Industry expected to benefit from technological advancement - adoption of cutting-edge technology promoting effective and sustainable production, reducing waste and improving production efficiency
- Global high-performance alloy market of USD 10.99 billion in CY 2025-26 projected to reach USD 18.52 billion by CY 2034, driven by additive manufacturing adoption, renewable energy expansion, electronics growth and demand for next-generation aircraft
- Global centrifugal casting market of USD 1.5 billion in CY 2025-26 projected to reach USD 2.2 billion by CY 2033, driven by automotive, aerospace, defence and industrial machinery demand
- Expanding use of high-performance alloys in oil and gas extraction, thermal processing, petroleum and power generation, including manufacturing of industrial gas turbine components, is expected to support industry growth in coming years
- Headwind flagged by management: tightening environmental regulations on emissions and waste could raise operating costs and affect industry performance
- Headwind flagged by management: the war in the Middle East threatens to disrupt growth and disinflation; tariffs, the war situation and linked commodity processes may create business-environment uncertainty affecting the financial position
- Record order book of approximately Rs.77 crore, described by management as providing strong visibility for future growth
- Secured the largest-ever project order from the fertilizer sector (largest-ever order from NFL)
- Won a major order for a petrochemical refinery in the MENA region; secured the highest-value customer order from the Middle East
- First-ever export order from the refinery segment
- First-time catalyst tube orders from both India and the MENA region
- Orders received from a major petroleum company and a leading DRI producer in the MENA region
- Expanded the customer base in the separation industry through new decanter centrifuge accounts
- Commercialised Thermalloy 64 MR reformer tubes through an order from a leading fertilizer company in India, and commercialised the new R-Alloy material with successful customer deliveries
- The Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) segment witnessed respectable growth in the order book

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Shift from component supplier to trusted engineering and materials solutions partner - recommending the right metallurgical solution and collaborating earlier in the customer's engineering cycle to create differentiated value in mission-critical applications
- Growth through applications rather than products: expand the application base of centrifugal castings into niche engineering sectors such as power generation, where material integrity, high-temperature performance and long service life are critical, and grow the separation (decanter centrifuge) business by leveraging metallurgical expertise into adjacent high-value applications
- Selective international expansion - focus on markets where technical capability offers clear differentiation (MENA, North America, Asia-Pacific) via deeper engagement with customers, EPC companies, technology licensors and process designers, rather than pursuing growth for its own sake
- Expand presence on global technology licensors' Approved Vendor Lists as a stated strategic priority, to strengthen credibility and gain access to larger international projects
- Capacity enhancement through the plant expansion (Bay-3) to support increasing demand from global markets and specialised applications
- Continued focus on automation, digital manufacturing and data-driven process control to improve productivity, consistency, quality and responsiveness; developing an end-to-end automated reformer production line and expanding low-cost automation
- Application-led R&D: next-generation alloy development, optimising reformer catalyst tubes for longer service life in fertiliser and refinery use, advanced alloys for ethylene and ammonia cracking, and development of proprietary heat-, wear- and corrosion-resistant alloys
- Digitalisation of the finance function - integrated reporting, enhanced analytics and an ongoing SAP implementation to strengthen controls, reporting accuracy and decision support
- Disciplined capital management: strategic asset monetisation (Thane land), prudent treasury management with proceeds deployed in mutual funds and fixed deposits, and disciplined investment evaluation
- Risk management embedded in financial strategy - active monitoring of raw material markets, strategic inventory positions, forex hedging, long-term supplier arrangements, and diversification across customers, geographies and end-use industries to reduce concentration risk
- People strategy - strengthen employer branding, develop specialised talent, expand campus hiring (METLeap), deepen engagement (METEngage survey), and run the Darwinbox HRMS across payroll, recruitment and performance
- Stated go-forward priorities: deepen customer partnerships, accelerate application-led innovation, strengthen manufacturing excellence and execute with discipline

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Board has approved a capital outlay of Rs.121 crore towards strengthening the Company's production and operational capabilities, described in the Chairman/CFO commentary as planned capital expenditure for FY 2026-27 focused on the Bay-3 expansion. Management frames this as capacity enhancement through plant expansion to support increasing demand from global markets and specialised applications, and points to significant value-creation opportunities from the Bay-3 expansion, automation initiatives, a new manufacturing facility and continued investments in specialised petrochemical and catalyst tube applications. Alongside the physical expansion, the Company is developing an end-to-end automated reformer production line, expanding low-cost automation and strengthening digital manufacturing capabilities to support future capacity expansion, with continued investment in automation, TPM, IoT-enabled Spectro analysis, digital quality systems and advanced welding technologies. A SAP implementation is under way to integrate operational and financial systems. On the operating side FY 2025-26 saw total pouring volume rise 11% to 4,172 MT with the highest melting output achieved in two consecutive months, pull-boring productivity improved from 8 to over 10 tubes per day, and 150 assemblies fabricated with 170 dispatched in March 2026. No commissioning date, completion date or capacity addition figure is disclosed for Bay-3 or for the new manufacturing facility, and R&D capital expenditure for the year is stated as Rs. Nil.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Recognised as a leading manufacturer of centrifugal castings in India, with deep expertise in heat-, wear- and corrosion-resistant alloy solutions and static castings for critical-use environments
- Over five decades of operating legacy (established 1972) and backing of the Neterwala Group, which spans Metallurgy, Software, Speciality Chemicals, Engineering, Geology, Oil & Gas and Environmental solutions
- R&D depth with active technical partnerships with IIT Bombay, IIT Madras, IIT Dharwad and IISc Bengaluru for advanced material characterisation and metallurgical research
- Qualification/approval barrier: actively pursuing product approvals and enlistments from leading global technology licensors, an entry barrier once secured
- High benchmarks on quality and on-time delivery described by management as providing a competitive edge; right-first-time manufacturing culture with operator self-inspection, in-process checks and process audits
- Manufacturing digitalisation and automation - IoT-enabled Spectro analysis, digital quality systems, advanced welding technologies, TPM, and an SQCDPR framework with OEE, MTBF, MTTR, material yield and OTIF KPIs
- Supply-chain resilience built deliberately: three independent LPG supply sources to guarantee zero production downtime, multi-sourcing of critical materials, strategic stockpiling and regional sourcing
- Process innovation lowering cost: optimised manufacturing processes to maximise utilisation of in-house generated materials and existing inventory, significantly reducing material costs while maintaining stringent quality standards
- Very low leverage and strong liquidity described qualitatively by management (Debt Equity 0.03 and Current Ratio 5.60 versus 0.08 and 2.69 in the prior year)

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Raw material price volatility — Management names volatility in raw material prices as one of the two key risks identified. Uni Abex's alloy castings are nickel- and other-alloy intensive, so input cost swings hit margins directly. Mitigation disclosed: sourcing from multiple suppliers to ensure supply continuity and cost-effective procurement, active monitoring of raw material markets, strategic inventory positions, strategic stockpiling of critical materials and long-term arrangements with major suppliers.
- Foreign exchange exposure on imports and exports — Foreign exchange rate movements may affect the Company's international business, including material imports and goods exports - a structural exposure given the deliberate push into MENA, North America and Asia-Pacific export markets. Mitigation disclosed: hedging measures through contractual arrangements, with forex exposures continuously reviewed.
- Macroeconomic and geopolitical shocks, including the Middle East conflict and tariffs — Management flags that unexpected shifts in the economic environment can impact operations and profitability, that the war in the Middle East threatens to disrupt growth and disinflation, and that material changes such as tariffs, the current war situation and linked commodity processes may put uncertainty in the business environment which may affect the financial position. The exposure is doubled-sided because MENA is both a target growth region and the source of the geopolitical disruption; energy commodity prices are projected to rise 19% in 2026 with oil up 21.4%.
- Tightening environmental regulation and carbon border compliance — Increasing environmental concerns and the tightening of related regulations are placing additional pressure on manufacturers, especially in managing emissions and waste, and compliance with these evolving norms could lead to higher operational costs which may affect overall industry performance. For an exporter this extends to carbon border regimes - the Company reports having achieved CBAM compliance during the year.
- Skilled technical manpower shortage, particularly welders — The Company reports having had to address skilled welder shortages by recruiting from technical institutes and providing 2-3 week structured on-the-job training to build an internal talent pool. With a total permanent workforce of only 103 employees as at 31 March 2026, availability of specialised welding and metallurgical skills is a genuine constraint on scaling output and on executing the planned Bay-3 expansion.
- Energy and critical-input supply disruption — The Company experienced LPG supply disruptions during the year and mitigated them by establishing three independent private supply sources to guarantee zero production downtime. Melting and heat-treatment operations are energy-intensive, so continuity of fuel and power supply is a direct production risk.
- Customer, geographic and end-use concentration with project-order cyclicality — Management explicitly cites diversification across customers, geographies and end-use industries as the means of reducing concentration risk and market cyclicality - an acknowledgement that the exposure exists. Revenue is driven by a relatively small number of large project orders (execution of large orders from NFL, NRL and CPCL named as a driver of the year's performance, against a record order book of approximately Rs.77 crore), and demand is concentrated in petrochemical, fertiliser and refinery reformer applications, making revenue lumpy and tied to those sectors' capex cycles.
- Broad business and economic risks identified by the Board — The Board's risk management policy states the Company, like all business in the country, is exposed to business and economic risks arising out of war, market conditions, vagaries of monsoon, tariffs and commodity risks. The Board has identified risks and steps to mitigate them, with the executive management operating an adequately defined risk-management framework.
